tool.name: cve_lookup
tool.description:
Query OSV.dev (the Open Source Vulnerability database) for known CVEs affecting a `(package_name, version, ecosystem)` triple. Designed to run right after `fingerprint_tech_stack` resolves a technology version — closes the loop between recon-time detection and the catalog of known-vulnerable releases without spending agent tokens.
Each `vulns[]` entry returned by OSV emits one finding tagged with the CVE ID. The tracer's existing KEV enrichment (CISA Known-Exploited-Vulnerabilities catalog) auto-decorates these findings with `is_kev=True`, `kev_due_date`, and `ransomware_use` flags — no extra integration needed in this tool.
Severity derivation: - `database_specific.severity` → GHSA enum (CRITICAL/HIGH/MODERATE/LOW) → mapped to (critical/high/medium/low). - `database_specific.cvss.score` → CVSS bands (>=9 critical / >=7 high / >=4 medium / else low). - `severity[].score` → numeric or vector. Numeric goes through CVSS bands; vector with `AV:N + AC:L` → high, otherwise medium. - Default: medium when no signal.
Caching: - Per-(ecosystem, name, version) JSON cache under `~/.strix/cve_lookup_cache/`, 6-hour TTL. - Stale cache served on network failure (fail-open). - Disable with `STRIX_CVE_LOOKUP_NO_CACHE=1`.
Composes with cluster-A safety: rate-limit applies to the OSV request. `--exclude-path` doesn't apply (URL is OSV.dev, not the customer's domain).
Recommended ecosystems for common fingerprint detections:
| Tech | Ecosystem | |---|---| | express / react / vue / angular / next / lodash / etc. | `npm` | | django / flask / fastapi / starlette | `PyPI` | | rails / sinatra | `RubyGems` | | spring / log4j / tomcat / struts / jackson | `Maven` | | laravel / symfony / drupal | `Packagist` | | gin / echo | `Go` | | actix / rocket | `crates.io` | | nginx / apache / IIS / WordPress core | (no clean OSV mapping — use empty string) |
For non-OSV-indexed software (server binaries, WordPress core), pass empty string for ecosystem; OSV will match by package name across ecosystems but coverage is limited.
Each finding carries `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (upgrade to the OSV-published fix-version OR monitor the advisory if no fix published) and `verification_status=verified` since OSV's data is authoritative.

parameter.name: name
parameter.description: Package name (e.g. `express`, `django`, `log4j-core`). For Maven packages, use the `groupId:artifactId` format (e.g. `org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core`).

parameter.name: version
parameter.description: Exact version string (e.g. `4.16.0`, `1.11.5`, `2.14.1`). Pre-release suffixes (`-rc.1`, `-beta`) preserved verbatim.

parameter.name: ecosystem
parameter.description: OSV ecosystem identifier. One of: `npm`, `PyPI`, `Maven`, `Go`, `RubyGems`, `crates.io`, `NuGet`, `Packagist`, `Hex`, `Pub`, `ConanCenter`, `SwiftURL`, plus Linux-distro names (`Debian`, `Ubuntu`, `Alpine`, etc.). Pass empty string to query without an ecosystem filter (OSV will match by name across ecosystems — lower precision but useful when the ecosystem is unknown).

returns.description:
{success, name, version, ecosystem, osv_url, queried_at, cve_count, from_cache, vulnerabilities: [{id, cve, severity, severity_source: {source, value?}, summary, fix_versions, references, ghsa_id, alias_count}, ...], findings_emitted, error?}.
The agent should: 1. Sort vulnerabilities by severity for prioritisation. 2. Highlight any CVE the tracer auto-tagged with `is_kev=True` (those are actively-exploited and fix-immediately). 3. When the same package has multiple matching CVEs, prioritise the one with the cleanest fix-path.
